To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the market values of computer investments are increased by organizational changes that are consistent with the computer’s potential to improve the efficiency of information processing in organizations.
the market value of a dollar of computer capital increases by a factor of 5.2 (or more) when it is accompanied by certain organizational characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of computers in the modern corporation.
the question of whether the value of a firm’s computer investments can be increased by the interaction of computers with the organizational structure of the firm.
the question of how computer investments affect a firm’s market valuation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of computer investments and organizational change is a critical factor in the success of computer investment.
computer investments are more valuable when they are combined in a particular way with organizational changes.
the interaction of computer investments and organizational structure is a critical determinant of a firm’s stock market value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
computers and organizational structure are complements.
the interaction between organizational factors and computer investments is critical to their economic success.
computer investments are not just investments in tangible assets; they are also investments in intangible assets, and the latter are important for understanding the value of computers to the firm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
computer investments do indeed create intangible assets.
the interaction of computers with the organizational structure is a critical determinant of the success of computer investment.
the interaction of computers with organizational structures is an important determinant of the value that firms derive from computer capital investments.
